# Startup readback: AI-41

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Harden the existing Windows worker device lifecycle and outbound task protocol, preserving its local-only role. Outcomes: (1) pairing, poll, heartbeat, result submission and revocation remain bound to a registered device and cannot be reused or replayed by another device; (2) claims, leases and revoked-device work follow the existing queue recovery contract; (3) the supported worker version/capabilities and device health are observable while the worker exposes no inbound listener and executes only its bounded signed action catalogue.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-12, AI-13, AI-18 and AI-19 are Done; completion evidence is AI-12 PR #162 (`9238c59b9c43688bf1e3736a4d041d57e5b4af25`), AI-13 PR #167 (`f7782239b2c08d273ea296420e80e5dee5361048`), and AI-19 PR #171 (`daae0525b7a06d897e045390d8d91297d3324276`), with AI-18's queue lease regression also merged. Existing contracts: authenticated-user JWT + fresh AAL2 MFA gate for site registration/revocation; per-device secret and Ed25519 public identity for outbound Edge calls; device-bound queue/lease ownership, audit/correlation and recovery. Using existing `worker-pair`, `worker-poll`, `worker-heartbeat`, `worker-submit-result`, `device-register`, `device-revoke`, shared `worker-auth`, and Windows worker client contracts; integration rules: DB-03, ACC-02, OPS-01 and new WORKER-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

The confirmed gap was protocol compatibility: the client did not send capability metadata, its advertised version diverged from package metadata, and poll did not reject unsupported workers before queue work. The shared Edge validator now requires the supported minimum version and inventory capability, rejects unknown capabilities before polling, and only offers signed actions when advertised. Heartbeat persists compatibility in the existing heartbeat status so the device UI can show upgrade/block reasons and capabilities. No migration was needed. Private keys remain device-bound, transport outbound HTTPS only, and action execution stays limited to typed signed manifests; no listener, arbitrary remote command execution, or auth/RLS/MFA changes were introduced.

## Local tests and commands

Focused proofs passed: `deno test --no-config supabase/functions/_shared/worker-protocol_test.ts` (4/4, including old-version rejection and missing inventory rejection), `deno check --config supabase/functions/deno.json` for both changed Edge functions, `python -m pytest -q apps/windows-worker/tests` (15/15), web typecheck, web tests (104/104), and web production build. The final `corepack pnpm verify:changed` passed: frontend checks, Edge formatting/lint/typecheck and 66 contract tests, Windows worker tests, and Chromium E2E (17/17). Its first attempt exposed readback formatting and Deno no-config import resolution; the import now pins `npm:zod@4.1.5`, the readback is formatted, and the regression plus integration-rule/ledger changes were included in the passing run.

## Hosted proof and readiness

AI-41 explicitly requires live staging sign-off: real Windows worker, fresh MFA via deployed device UI, paired device identity/version/capabilities, Edge poll/heartbeat/result correlation, harmless task completion, cross-device/replay denial, immediate revoke plus safe outstanding-task recovery, fresh re-pair with old credentials still revoked, outbound-only OS/network inspection, and clear block for outdated/incompatible capabilities. The device/MFA browser action is operator-owned: pause before sign-in and notify parent when the headed browser is ready; wait for their user-action request. No live sign-off is claimed yet. After staging proof, complete required CI, merge, bounded production smoke, and post `LIVE E2E SIGN-OFF: PASS` only when every declared step has evidence.

## Delegation and blockers

Single owner is this AI-41 lane through merge and Linear Done; no subagent handoffs. Frozen install and `corepack pnpm qa:doctor --fix` passed at base SHA `2c7884ff00f177e2974e01a2c5b05e97178c038b`. The final changed-surface gate is green. Next action: commit and open the PR, monitor CI, then promote the exact candidate and prepare the operator-owned live staging sign-off. Live staging/MFA still requires parent/operator participation and a real Windows device.
